content.title: About
content.content: Black plum (Prunus domestica) is a variety of plum characterized by its dark, almost black skin and sweet, juicy flesh. Raw fruits are eaten fresh and are also used in cooking for jams, compotes, and desserts. Plums are rich in vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black plums are often called “black‑fruit plum”; their dark color is due to high anthocyanin content.
Plums belong to the Rosaceae family and are closely related to peaches, apricots, and cherries.
Raw plums can be used to make homemade vinegar and tinctures.
The dark skin of plums contains more polyphenols than lighter varieties.
In ancient cultures, plums symbolized fertility and abundance.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: The dark skin provides anthocyanins and flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Dietary fiber promotes regular bowel movements and helps prevent constipation.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Potassium and magnesium help regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Raw plums are low‑calorie, making them a good choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to plums.

items.title: Cyanogenic glycosides in pits
items.content: Plum pits contain amygdalin, which can release cyanide when crushed; pits should not be eaten in large amounts.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Raw plums can be quite acidic and may irritate the stomach of people with high gastric acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw black plums can be eaten fresh, added to salads, smoothies, yogurt, or used for jams and compotes. The skin is edible and rich in antioxidants, though it can be peeled if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store plums in the refrigerator in an airtight container for 5‑7 days. For longer storage, freeze the berries on a tray, then transfer to a freezer bag.
